newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel barges close shade higher, cargoes steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel barges close shade higher, cargoes steady.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges closed on Friday a shade higher but off highs seen during the week, while low sulphur cargoes were still offered at high numbers, traders said.
High sulphur cargoes seemed steady while one percent was offered at steady prices but no deals were struck.
High sulphur barges fetched $82.50 fob ARA in the late afternoon, or $1 over Thursday's closing level, and after trading earlier in the day at $81, and as low as $79.50 and $79 in the early morning.
Traders said the numbers began on the low side as a trading house wanting to price a cargo tried to drive the market down.
"Demand is not too bad and availability has thinned, but pricing is involved...All prices you hear are related to an interest that people have in bringing it up or down," the trader added.
Bunkers were heard done at $83/$84 a tonne for 380 CST and $88/$89 for 180 CST, traders said.
Low sulphur barges were still offered by three or four sellers at last done, or $96 a tonne and buyers moved up from the low nineties to about $94 a tonne.
High sulphur cargoes seemed steady to a shade stronger with a Russian cracked reported traded at about two means, or $1 higher than its asking price a day earlier.
"That seems more or less a market price," one trader said.

One percent was still offered by a U.K. refiner at $94.50 but no deal was done with two buyers seen at $93/$94 a tonne. A second refiner was heard to have a cargo on offer but no details were available.
Traders said the market would probably come off a bid early next week as it had stayed at this level without any deals done.
"Low sulphur is not looking too great. There are two cargoes to go and not a huge number of buyers," a trader said.
